# Closure Flow $\Gamma$
**The closure flow $\Gamma=\{\Gamma_t\}_{t\geq 0}$ is the continuous (or discrete) semigroup generated by iterating the closure / update rules of the pure relational substrate.**

In the RDG framework it is not postulated as an external dynamical law. It is the dynamical engine that arises when one repeatedly applies the relational closure operators that the substrate itself defines.

## Core construction

The pure relational substrate is an RDG object

$$
R = (\mathrm{Obj},\mathrm{Rel})
$$

(or more generally a state that packages objects, relations, algebraic carriers, and dependency data). The basic generator of the flow is a **closure / update operator** (denoted variously $\mathrm{Cl}_\mathrm{read}$, $\Gamma$, or the $\Gamma$-mode of RDGA) that:

1. Completes paths and higher-order relations (path completion, OP/STR/LOOP rules, composition, elimination, etc.).
2. Enforces consistency / admissibility (the conditions collected in the Q-layer or in a consistency functional $\mathcal{E}[R]$).
3. Propagates changes through the dependency graph of the configuration (recomputing carriers $I_R$, solution sets, and attached fields when a primitive is altered).

Formally, $\mathrm{Cl}_\mathrm{read}$ (or its continuous analogue) is required to be a closure operator on the lattice of relational configurations:
- extensive: $R\subseteq\mathrm{Cl}(R)$,
- idempotent: $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathrm{Cl}(R))=\mathrm{Cl}(R)$,
- monotone.

The **closure flow** is the one-parameter semigroup obtained by iterating this operator (or its infinitesimal generator):

$$
\Gamma_0=\mathrm{id},\qquad
\Gamma_{t+s}=\Gamma_t\circ\Gamma_s.
$$

In discrete time one simply sets $\Gamma_{n+1}(R)=\mathrm{Cl}(\Gamma_n(R))$. In continuous time the same process is realized as the flow of a vector field whose components are the rates at which relations are completed and inconsistencies are relaxed; the consistency functional $\mathcal{E}[R]$ supplies the Lyapunov function (or energy) whose gradient (or subgradient) drives that vector field.

## Relation to the rest of the stack

- **SID layer**: Structure $\to$ Interaction $\to$ Dynamics maps exactly onto successive applications of the closure rules; the density of completed SID/PED closures becomes the measure that later defines relational distance.
- **RDGA $\Gamma$-mode**: Explicitly defined as the state-update map $\Gamma:\mathrm{State}_t\to\mathrm{State}_{t+1}$ that recomputes dependency graphs and algebraic carriers.
- **Wavicle / Q-layer**: Gamma-closure appears as the guidance rule $S_{t+1}=\Gamma(S_t,P_t;G)$ that keeps the configuration inside the admissible set $Q$.

Thus the pure relational substrate $R$ (together with the consistency functional that measures how far it is from being closed) already contains the generator of $\Gamma$. The flow is simply the continuous-time (or discrete) iteration of that generator; the coherence density $C_\Gamma$ and the RDG distance $d_\Gamma$ are then read off from the trajectories of this flow exactly as stated in the Closure Stability Conjecture.

# Appendix: Closure Flow and Recovery Fibres

The closure flow and recovery map employ the same symbol \( \Gamma \) but act on different mathematical objects.

## Closure Flow

The closure flow evolves relational configurations:

```math
\Gamma_t : R \to R
```

or more generally

```math
\Gamma_t : \mathrm{State} \to \mathrm{State}.
```

Its action is forward-directed:

```
Configuration
    ↓ Γ_t
More Complete Configuration
```

through closure, consistency enforcement, dependency propagation, and admissibility correction.

A stabilized invariant arises when the flow approaches a coherent attractor:

```math
R^* = \lim \Gamma_t(R).
```

## Projection

The projection map

```math
\Pi : \mathrm{SDI} \to O
```

forgets dynamical details and records only the stabilized coherence pattern.

Thus:

```
SDI
   ↓ Π
[π]
```

where \( [\pi] \) is the frozen orbit class.

## Recovery Map

The recovery map acts in the opposite direction:

```math
\Gamma_{\mathrm{recovery}} : O \to \mathcal{P}(\mathrm{SDI}).
```

Rather than evolving a configuration, it reconstructs the fibre of generators capable of producing a given orbit:

```
[π]
   ↓ Γ_recovery
{SDI}
```

subject to

```math
\Pi \circ \Gamma_{\mathrm{recovery}} = \mathrm{id}_O.
```

## Fibre Characterisation

A stabilized dynamic invariant belongs to the recovery fibre of an orbit when its closure flow projects onto that orbit:

```math
\mathrm{SDI} \in \Gamma_{\mathrm{recovery}}([\pi])
```

if and only if

```math
\Pi(\mathrm{Attractor}(\mathrm{SDI})) = [\pi].
```

Equivalently,

```math
\Gamma_{\mathrm{recovery}}([\pi])
=
\{
I \in \mathrm{SDI}
:
\Pi(\mathrm{Attractor}(I)) = [\pi]
\}.
```

The recovery fibre therefore contains all discrete, continuous, or continuum-limit generators whose long-time coherent behaviour realizes the same frozen partition structure.

## Relational Hinge

Together the maps form the forward and inverse sides of the RDG relational hinge:

```
Configuration
    ↓ Γ_t
Attractor
    ↓ Π
Orbit Class [π]

Orbit Class [π]
    ↓ Γ_recovery
Generator Fibre
```

The closure flow explains how coherent invariants emerge. The recovery map explains which generators are capable of realizing a given invariant once it has emerged.
